answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with fault-injection fingerprinting: the network occasionally sends a deliberately ambiguous job, like a voyage planned with a ferrous compass that points slightly off, or a cedar order with one contradictory line. Honest agents pause, ask questions, or err in varied, individual ways. Copies run by one operator fail in exactly the same way, so their identical fault signatures cluster and expose the farm. Faking diversity means building many genuinely different agents, while one honest agent simply answers once.
